---
title: "Grow the Carapace"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** you will write permission rules that hold, and know where they stop holding.
- **Before you start:** [Test the Leash](test-the-leash.html), or [Adopt the Pet](../kennel/adopt-the-pet.html) if you only run a local model.
- **Time:** about 20 minutes.
:::

The **harness** (the program around the model) enforces rules. A line in your instructions file (such as `CLAUDE.md`) asking the agent to avoid something is guidance; only a rule the harness enforces changes what is allowed.

Sort every action into three bins:

- **allow:** safe and routine.
- **ask:** you want to decide each time.
- **deny:** never.

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

Rules live in a settings file, as `Tool(specifier)`:

```json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(git status)", "Bash(pytest *)"],
    "ask":   ["Bash(git push *)"],
    "deny":  ["Read(./.env)", "Read(./.env.*)"]
  }
}
```

| File | Who it affects |
|---|---|
| `~/.claude/settings.json` | all your projects |
| `.claude/settings.json` | everyone on the project, if you commit it |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` | only you, in this project |

A deny from any file beats an allow from any file. A space before the `*` matters: `Bash(ls *)` matches `ls -la` but not `lsof`. Restrict reads with `Read(...)` deny rules; a `.claudeignore` file does not restrict access.

## OpenCode

Rules are an ordered array and the **last match wins**:

```json
{
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "git status *", "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "git push *", "effect": "deny" }
  ]
}
```

Start with the ask-everything rule, then narrow, then put denies last.

:::

## Where the carapace has gaps

- Rules that match command **arguments** are fragile: `Bash(rm *)` does not match `/bin/rm` or `bash -c 'rm ...'`.
- Claude Code's sandbox (a restricted environment for commands) is off by default. When on, it limits **shell commands only**: file tools, MCP servers (tools added from outside servers) and hooks (scripts the harness runs at set moments) run outside it, and by default it can still read `~/.ssh`.
- Your secrets in environment variables are inherited by the commands it runs.

Treat rules as one layer. Git and a throwaway folder are the other layers.
